mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, the Exalted, {تَنْزِيل من الرَّحْمَن الرَّحِيم}: تنزيل is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); من الرحمن is its naʿt (adjective), الرحيم a second naʿt, and كتاب its khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ said: it is nominative by an implied هذا ("this is").

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {قُرْآنًا عَرَبيا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial). It has also been said that it is accusative as praise (madḥ). Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ did not allow it to be accusative as a ḥāl; rather, according to them it is accusative by فصّلت, i.e. "its verses have been detailed thus". In (ordinary) speech they both allowed the nominative, as a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying {بشيرا وَنَذِيرا}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from الآيات, and what governs all the ḥāls is فصّلت. It is also possible that بشيرا ونذيرا are two ḥāls from كتاب, because it has been given an adjective; what governs the ḥāl is then the sense of the implied drawing of attention (tanbīh), or the sense of pointing, if you take the implied form to be "this is a Book whose verses have been detailed".

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying {يُوحى إِلَيّ أَنما}: أنّ is in the nominative position, governed by يوحى.

His saying سواء is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of استواء, i.e. "they were equal, an equalness". Whoever put it in the nominative took it as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with للسائلين as the khabar (predicate), in the sense of "equal for whoever asked and said: in how many (days) were they created?". It has also been said: "for whoever asks" means for all creation, because they ask for sustenance and other things from Allah, exalted be His mention. Whoever put it in the genitive made it a naʿt (adjective) of الأيام or of أربعة. The well-known readers have the accusative only.

[Translator's note: سواء is in āya 10, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying {أَتَيْنَا طائعين}: He reported about the heavens and the earths with the yāʾ and nūn (the masculine sound plural used for rational beings), according to the Kufans and al-Kisāʾī, only because the meaning is "we came, with those within us, obedient"; so He reported about rational beings with the yāʾ and nūn, which is the basic rule. It has also been said that since He reported about them with speech, which belongs to rational beings, He reported about them as about rational beings, with the yāʾ and nūn.

[Translator's note: the source has «السوات», evidently for «السماوات», and «أخبر عنها من يعقل», evidently for «أخبر عنها إخبار من يعقل».]

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {فقضاهن سبع سماوات}: سبع is a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ and nūn, i.e. "He completed seven heavens". السماء is treated as masculine in the sense of "roof", and is also treated as feminine. The Qurʾān came with the feminine, saying سبع سماوات; had it come with the masculine, it would have said سبعة سماوات.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {وَأما ثَمُود فهديناهم}: ثمود is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is not fully declined (a diptote) because it is definite, the name of the tribe. [Translator's note: the source has «اسم للصلة», evidently a misprint for «اسم للقبيلة».] Al-Aʿmash read it fully declined, making it the name of the clan. It is related from al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim that they read it in the accusative without full declension, putting it in the accusative by an implied verb which فهديناهم explains, because أمّا carries the meaning of condition and is therefore more suited to the verb. So the accusative, for him, is stronger; but the nominative is fully good, and it is the preferred view according to Sībawayh. The implied form of the accusative is "whatever may be the case, We guided Thamūd: We guided them".

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying {وَيَوْم يحْشر أَعدَاء الله إِلَى النَّار}: what governs يوم is a verb indicated by يوزعون, its implied form being "and people are driven on the day when (the enemies of Allah) are gathered", or "and remember the day…". يحشر does not govern it, because يوم is in construct with it, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying {تستترون أَن يشْهد}: أن is in the accusative position by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "from (عن) that (your hearing) should testify" or "from (من) that it should testify".

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying {وذلكم ظنكم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and أرداكم a second khabar. It has also been said that ظنكم is a badal (substitute) for ذلكم and أرداكم the khabar. Al-Farrāʾ said أرداكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial); but according to the Basrans a past verb is not good as a ḥāl except with قد implied.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying {ذَلِك جَزَاء أَعدَاء الله النَّار}: ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and جزاء its khabar (predicate), and النار is (a badal) from جزاء. It has also been said that النار is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, the clause being in the position of an explanation (bayān) of the first clause.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t: His saying نزلا: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it has also been said that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:39-39.t:
His saying {وَمن آيَاته أَنَّك}: أنّ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the prepositional phrase before it is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. It has also been said that أنّ is nominative by the (implied) "being settled" (istiqrār). Beginning with the fatḥa-form (أنّ) is permissible because the genitive phrase precedes it.

His saying {خاشعة} is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الأرض, because ترى is from seeing with the eye.

His saying {وربت}: the final radical (lām al-fiʿl) of the verb was dropped because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the feminine tāʾ. It is from ربا يربو, when something increases; from it comes الربا, (usury) in debt, which is forbidden. Abū Jaʿfar read وربأت with hamza, from الربيئة, which is elevation, so its meaning is "it rose". One says ربأ يربأ and ربؤ يربؤ when something rises.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {إِن الَّذين كفرُوا بِالذكر لما جَاءَهُم}: the khabar (predicate) of إنّ is أولئك ينادون. It has also been said that the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "those who disbelieved in the Reminder when it came to them have lost" or "have been destroyed", and the like.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His saying {إِلَّا مَا قد قيل للرسل}: مَا with the verb is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the nominative position as the object whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent) of يقال, because the verb reaches the maṣdar, so the maṣdar is made to stand in place of the agent. Even if (a verb) does not take an object, it does reach the maṣdar and adverbs.

mekki-muskil:44-44.t:
His saying {وَالَّذين لَا يُؤمنُونَ فِي آذانهم وقر}: الذين is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows is its khabar (predicate); وقر is a mubtadaʾ and في آذانهم its khabar, and لا يؤمنون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين.

His saying {يتَبَيَّن لَهُم أَنه الْحق}: the hāʾ in أنه is for Allah the Exalted; it has also been said for the Qurʾān, and it has been said for the Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace. أنّ is in the nominative position, governed by يتبيّن, because it is its fāʿil (agent).

[Translator's note: يتبين لهم أنه الحق is in āya 53, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:45-45.t: His saying {وَلَوْلَا كلمة}: كلمة is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted and is not made overt, according to Sībawayh.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {من أكمامها}: it is the plural of كِمّ; and whoever says أكمّة makes it the plural of كِمام.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {أولم يكف بِرَبِّك أَنه}: بربك is in the nominative position because it is the fāʿil (agent) of يكف, and أنه is a badal (substitute) for ربك according to its position, so it is in the nominative position; or it is in the genitive position as a badal according to the wording. It has also been said that it is in the accusative position by omission of the lām, i.e. "because He is over all things (a witness)".
